prompt: Explain how a standing wave forms on a string fixed at both ends, and state one way it differs from a travelling wave.
markscheme: Waves reflected from the ends superpose with the incident waves: two identical waves travelling in opposite directions **(R1)**. A standing wave transfers no net energy along the string (or: has nodes and antinodes, with amplitude varying with position) **(A1)**

prompt: Points P and Q lie on a standing wave, in adjacent loops (one node between them). What is their phase difference?
markscheme: **C.** All points between two adjacent nodes oscillate in phase; points in neighbouring loops oscillate in antiphase ($\pi$ rad), whatever their amplitudes.

concept: Standing waves in strings and pipes
prompt:
**(a)** A string 0.80 m long fixed at both ends carries waves at $240\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the fundamental frequency and the frequency of the third harmonic. **[2]**

**(b)** A pipe of length 0.34 m is closed at one end. Calculate its two lowest resonant frequencies. (Speed of sound $=340\ \text{m s}^{-1}$) **[2]**

**(c)** State the lowest frequency if the pipe is open at both ends. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\lambda_1=2L=1.6$ m, $f_1=150$ Hz **(A1)**; $f_3=450$ Hz **(A1)**

**(b)** Node at the closed end, antinode at the open end: $\lambda_1=4L=1.36$ m, $f_1=250$ Hz **(A1)**; only odd harmonics, so next is 750 Hz **(A1)**

**(c)** $\lambda=2L$: 500 Hz **(A1)**

prompt: Explain what is meant by resonance and give one example where it is useful.
markscheme: When a system is driven at a frequency equal (or very close) to its natural frequency, energy is transferred most efficiently and the amplitude becomes maximum **(R1)**. Useful e.g. in musical instruments, microwave ovens, tuning a radio, MRI **(A1)**

prompt: Describe how increasing the damping of a driven oscillator changes its graph of amplitude against driving frequency.
markscheme: The peak amplitude is lower and the peak is broader **(A1)**; the frequency of maximum amplitude moves slightly below the natural frequency **(A1)**

prompt: A car's suspension is designed to be critically damped. Describe light, critical and heavy damping, and explain why critical damping is chosen.
markscheme:
Light: oscillates with gradually decreasing amplitude; heavy: returns to equilibrium very slowly without oscillating **(A1)**; critical: returns to equilibrium in the shortest time without oscillating **(A1)**

After a bump the car settles quickly without bouncing (comfort and road grip) **(R1)**
